findings.title: q-dir@12.84: hash check failed
findings.summary_md: A Scoop Extras report says the Q-Dir 12.84 portable archive downloaded from SoftwareOK's unversioned URL failed Scoop's SHA-256 check. The manifest expected `3a64bb681c2d46d1881063cd100ab16aa0b07641a4e02e7614cb51ce0746e055`, while the server returned `b634a9a9a43c51f7488aa10a12e11370c7ba5c541adc6a075490768ce6c7706a`.

findings.title: q-dir@12.84: hash check failed
findings.summary_md: A second Scoop Extras report recorded another Q-Dir 12.84 hash failure from the same SoftwareOK portable archive URL. Scoop expected `b634a9a9a43c51f7488aa10a12e11370c7ba5c541adc6a075490768ce6c7706a` but received `3a64bb681c2d46d1881063cd100ab16aa0b07641a4e02e7614cb51ce0746e055`, reversing the mismatch direction recorded on November 13.

findings.title: q-dir@12.84: download URL now serves a trojanized executable (remote access trojan) – please block the manifest
findings.summary_md: A Scoop Extras user reported that SoftwareOK's unversioned Q-Dir 12.84 portable download served a trojanized, unsigned executable and asked maintainers to block the manifest rather than accept its new hash. The report describes a machine infected after a build accepted during November 13-15, with `dsv2_py39_agent.7z` installed under `C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\DeviceSync\b2`, persistence and TCP traffic to `8.210.69.51:9876`; it lists remote shell, file transfer, screenshots and tunneling. It also supplies SHA-256 values for the malicious archive and embedded executable.
